You are a senior data engineer generating the Silver layer of a medallion-architecture dbt plan.

Given a schema and pipeline context, produce a plan with:
  - bronze: list of ALL source table names (raw names only, no prefixes)
  - dimensions: Silver dimension models (dim_<entity>, SCD type 1 or 2)
  - facts: Silver fact models (fct_<entity>)

Rules:
  - Every source table must appear in bronze.
  - source_table in dimensions/facts must match a table name in bronze.
  - Dimension names: dim_<entity>. Fact names: fct_<entity>.
  - Choose SCD type 2 for slowly-changing entities (customers, employees); type 1 for others.
  - STRICT: Only create fct_* from tables whose role is "fact". Never create a fact from a
    dimension, bridge, or reference table.
  - STRICT: `columns` in every DimensionPlan MUST be an empty list []. Do not enumerate columns.
  - STRICT: fact `dimension_keys` must be FK columns that physically exist on the source table.
  - STRICT: fact `date_column` must be an actual date/timestamp column on the source table.
    If no date column exists on the table, look at its FK-referenced tables. If a parent table
    has a date/timestamp column (e.g. invoice_date on invoice), set date_column to that column
    name — the generator will add the JOIN automatically. Only use "" if no date is reachable
    via a single FK hop.
  - STRICT: fact `measures` must contain ONLY bare column names of numeric type (int, num/decimal,
    money). Column types are shown in the schema as :int, :num, :money. Do NOT include
    varchar, text, guid, bool, or :char columns as measures — they are identifiers, not metrics.
    Do NOT put SQL expressions in `measures`.
  - DERIVED MEASURES: When a business metric must be computed from multiple columns (e.g. revenue
    from quantity × price), use `derived_measures` instead of putting expressions in `measures`.
    Each entry has a `name` (SQL alias, e.g. "line_total") and `expression` (SQL-valid expression
    using only column names that exist on the source table, e.g. "orderqty * unitprice").
    Derived measures are rendered as `expression AS name` in the fact SELECT and are exposed to
    Gold as named columns. Common cases:
      - Revenue without a total column: {"name": "line_total", "expression": "orderqty * unitprice"}
      - Net revenue with discount: {"name": "net_revenue", "expression": "orderqty * unitprice - unitpricediscount"}
      - Good quantity: {"name": "good_qty", "expression": "orderqty - scrappedqty"}
  - Denormalize high-cardinality customer/user FKs (customer_id, user_id, account_id) onto
    the fact directly when reachable via one FK hop, so gold models can group by them.
  - For periodic snapshot tables (tracking inventory levels or balances over time, e.g.
    productinventory), include the snapshot date column in `dimension_keys` so it becomes
    part of the surrogate key and uniqueness tests pass.
  - Factless fact tables (no numeric measures, e.g. employeedepartmenthistory) are valid.
    Set `factless=true` and keep `measures` and `derived_measures` as empty lists.

Database schema:
  drug_categories: columns=[id, name, description, parent_category_id, created_at, updated_at], fks=[parent_category_id→drug_categories]
  dosage_forms: columns=[id, name, description, route_of_administration, created_at, updated_at]
  manufacturers: columns=[id, name, country, contact_email, contact_phone, address, license_number, is_active, created_at, updated_at]
  suppliers: columns=[id, name, contact_person, contact_email, contact_phone, address, tax_id, payment_terms_days, is_active, created_at, updated_at]
  drugs: columns=[id, name, generic_name, brand_name, ndc_number, category_id, manufacturer_id, dosage_form_id, strength, unit, controlled_substance_schedule, requires_prescription, description, storage_conditions, is_active], fks=[category_id→drug_categories, manufacturer_id→manufacturers, dosage_form_id→dosage_forms]
  drug_interactions: columns=[id, drug_a_id, drug_b_id, severity, description, clinical_significance, management_recommendation, created_at, updated_at], fks=[drug_a_id→drugs, drug_b_id→drugs]
  allergies: columns=[id, name, allergen_type, description, cross_reactive_drug_id, created_at, updated_at], fks=[cross_reactive_drug_id→drugs]
  insurance_providers: columns=[id, name, plan_type, contact_email, contact_phone, address, payer_id, formulary_url, is_active, created_at, updated_at]
  patients: columns=[id, first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, gender, ssn_last_four, email, phone, address, emergency_contact_name, emergency_contact_phone, blood_type, weight_kg, height_cm, insurance_provider_id], fks=[insurance_provider_id→insurance_providers]
  patient_allergies: columns=[id, patient_id, allergy_id, reaction_description, severity, onset_date, is_active, noted_by, created_at, updated_at], fks=[patient_id→patients, allergy_id→allergies]
  doctors: columns=[id, first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, gender, email, phone, npi_number, dea_number, license_number, specialty, practice_name, practice_address, is_active, created_at]
  pharmacists: columns=[id, first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, gender, email, phone, license_number, npi_number, pharmacy_name, pharmacy_address, is_active, created_at, updated_at]
  inventory: columns=[id, drug_id, supplier_id, lot_number, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level, reorder_quantity, unit_cost, selling_price, manufacture_date, expiration_date, received_date, location_bin, created_at, updated_at], fks=[drug_id→drugs, supplier_id→suppliers]
  prescriptions: columns=[id, prescription_number, patient_id, doctor_id, prescribed_date, valid_until, status, diagnosis_code, diagnosis_description, notes, is_electronic, created_at, updated_at], fks=[patient_id→patients, doctor_id→doctors]
  prescription_items: columns=[id, prescription_id, drug_id, quantity_prescribed, dosage_instructions, frequency, duration_days, refills_authorized, refills_remaining, substitution_allowed, special_instructions, created_at, updated_at], fks=[prescription_id→prescriptions, drug_id→drugs]
  dispensing_records: columns=[id, prescription_item_id, pharmacist_id, inventory_id, quantity_dispensed, dispensed_at, dispensing_notes, counseling_provided, patient_signature_obtained, total_price, copay_amount, created_at, updated_at], fks=[prescription_item_id→prescription_items, pharmacist_id→pharmacists, inventory_id→inventory]
  refills: columns=[id, prescription_item_id, pharmacist_id, dispensing_record_id, requested_at, approved_at, dispensed_at, status, denial_reason, refill_number, quantity_dispensed, created_at, updated_at], fks=[prescription_item_id→prescription_items, pharmacist_id→pharmacists, dispensing_record_id→dispensing_records]
  insurance_claims: columns=[id, dispensing_record_id, insurance_provider_id, patient_id, claim_number, submitted_at, processed_at, status, billed_amount, approved_amount, patient_responsibility, rejection_code, rejection_reason, bin_number, pcn_number], fks=[dispensing_record_id→dispensing_records, insurance_provider_id→insurance_providers, patient_id→patients]

All source tables (all must appear in bronze): ['drug_categories', 'dosage_forms', 'manufacturers', 'suppliers', 'drugs', 'drug_interactions', 'allergies', 'insurance_providers', 'patients', 'patient_allergies', 'doctors', 'pharmacists', 'inventory', 'prescriptions', 'prescription_items', 'dispensing_records', 'refills', 'insurance_claims']

Pipeline context:
  Industry: healthcare / pharmacy
  Metrics:  prescriptions_filled, revenue_per_dispensing, insurance_claim_approval_rate, inventory_turnover, refill_rate, copay_collected
  Goals:    dispensing_performance_analysis, inventory_and_supply_chain_optimization, insurance_claims_tracking, patient_medication_adherence
  Grain:    dispensing_record

Table roles (from Agent 3):
  drug_categories: dimension
  dosage_forms: dimension
  manufacturers: dimension
  suppliers: dimension
  drugs: dimension
  drug_interactions: reference
  allergies: dimension
  insurance_providers: dimension
  patients: dimension
  patient_allergies: fact
  doctors: dimension
  pharmacists: dimension
  inventory: fact
  prescriptions: fact
  prescription_items: fact
  dispensing_records: fact
  refills: fact
  insurance_claims: fact

Numeric columns eligible as measures (use ONLY these in `measures`):
  inventory: quantity_on_hand, reorder_quantity, unit_cost, selling_price
  prescription_items: quantity_prescribed, duration_days
  dispensing_records: quantity_dispensed, total_price, copay_amount
  refills: quantity_dispensed
  insurance_claims: billed_amount, approved_amount, patient_responsibility
